analysis: Reviewed CHANGELOG.md (head-only text, historical release notes; no security behavior change) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new 'Model startup calibration' section; the :0 unit has no visible content, only metadata). The doc describes startup calibration: a local-only EngineMeasurementPurpose.startupWarmup one-token health check, plus idle-time calibration probes (128-token warmup, two solo probes of at most 512 prompt / 32 output tokens) run through EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration. Calibration is cancelled by foreground customer requests (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.beginForeground), and EngineV2.submitWithRetirement holds KV/service reservations until stream retirement. Requires idle, nominal thermal state, not Low Power. Probes use synthetic prompts, not consumer data, and produce no billing counters. The probes are uncached and the doc states they seed solo rates only, so no new T-041 prefix-cache exposure is visible. Calibration evidence is published via capacity heartbeats; the coordinator treats those as provider-reported, so manipulation is bounded by the existing T-007/T-027 assumptions. No code is changed in this batch. A follow-up pass should check the actual Swift implementation (EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibration.swift, IdleCalibrationCoordinator.swift) for retirement/KV release, cache-donation exclusion, and whether calibrated rates can influence routing. No threat-model gap is evident from documentation alone.
